tested_scope: Exactly two raw strings: sample 0123456789abcdef repeated four times (64 lowercase hex code points), and the identical 64-code-point sample followed by U+000D U+000A. Acceptance rule is raw length exactly 64 and every raw code point in [0-9a-f], evaluated before any trim/normalization.
mechanism_claim_exact_scope: A checkpoint/state pointer digest parser that validates the raw transport string for exact length 64 plus lowercase-hex alphabet before normalization deterministically rejects a CRLF-suffixed digest while accepting the canonical digest. This is evidence only for this raw-string grammar boundary; it does not establish end-to-end transport integrity or behavior of regex engines/decoders that normalize input.
state_reconstruction_relevance: Rejecting raw suffix mutation prevents a reconstructed continuation from silently treating a transport-modified digest identity as the canonical checkpoint identity. The check is local, deterministic, replayable across runs, and needs only lightweight repository state transport.
conflict_check: own namespace only; no O, downstream, other-worker, legacy, shared-ledger, or other-role semantics consumed
exact_next_action: Test the adjacent raw suffix boundary: canonical lowercase 64-hex versus the same digest followed by LF only (U+000A), explicitly comparing an exact-length/raw-alphabet validator with any candidate full-string regex/anchor formulation. Precommit canonical accept and LF-suffixed reject; do not normalize. If engine-specific anchor behavior is asserted, source-qualify it from a public primary specification before broadening the claim.
